content: Rifapentine is specifically indicated for the treatment of pulmonary tuberculosis caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It is essential that rifapentine is always administered in combination with one or more antituberculosis drugs to which the causative organism is susceptible. The choice of combination therapy depends on the phase of treatment being undertaken. Rifapentine should not be used as a once-weekly continuation phase regimen in combination with isoniazid for HIV-positive patients with pulmonary tuberculosis. This is due to an increased risk of treatment failure and/or relapse, which has been associated with the emergence of rifampin-resistant organisms in such cases. The use of rifapentine as part of the initial phase treatment regimen in HIV-positive patients with pulmonary tuberculosis has not been studied, and therefore its efficacy and safety in this context remain unestablished. Rifapentine must not be used as monotherapy during either the initial or continuation phases of antituberculosis treatment, as this approach is not effective and could lead to treatment failure or resistance.
